source.title: MoVE: Mixture of Value Embeddings - A New Axis for Scaling Parametric Memory in Autoregressive Models

record.tranche_reason: The study varies added memory capacity and reports held-out validation BPB for text models, bearing on how loss changes with parameter count. It does not fit or test a power-law curve.
record.gate_note: The text-generation tables report held-out BPB across memory configurations and model depths; those results are recorded below. Image-generation results use FID and other image-quality measures, not held-out text loss. The ablation and routing analyses do not measure the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study assumes published scaling laws as motivation and benchmarks a new memory architecture. Its loss reductions do not establish power-law form, extrapolation, compute-optimal allocation, or fit dependence. Its architecture comparisons do not hold total parameters fixed across a wide range of shapes. None of V1–V7 is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate for the text experiments but narrower than the authors' overall conclusion. They conclude that shared value-embedding memory enables sustained capacity gains across text generation, image generation, and MLA with low arithmetic overhead. They acknowledge memory-bandwidth costs and lower gain per added parameter than standard dense scaling. They report no fitted power law.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains MoVE and LaVE variants and reports validation BPB rather than fitting the original scaling-law relationships among model size, tokens, compute, or compute-optimal allocations.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported text BPB varies with model depth, memory architecture, memory-slot multiplier, and attention architecture (standard attention or MLA).

fits_no_version.finding: MoVE lowers held-out text BPB as its memory bank grows, including under MLA. D12 standard-attention BPB falls from 0.838 to 0.797; D12 MLA falls from 0.8826 to 0.8690.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing a shared value-embedding memory bank can improve text compression at fixed backbone depth and training-token exposure.

fits_no_version.finding: Layer-wise memory improves standard-attention BPB, but doubling its capacity under MLA slightly worsens BPB on both tested depths.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The effectiveness of additional value-embedding memory depends on its architecture.

fits_no_version.finding: MoVE improves ImageNet generation FID from 6.53 to 5.62 for GPT-B and from 3.47 to 3.10 for GPT-L.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Shared value-embedding memory can improve autoregressive image-generation quality at the tested model sizes.

record.problems: The text experiments use three model depths and a reserved final dataset shard; the paper states that the experiments are at scales significantly smaller than commercial foundation models. No uncertainty estimates or power-law fits are reported. Training-token exposure is fixed across variants, not swept.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 image-generation results use FID, IS, precision, and recall rather than held-out text loss. Table 4 compares architectural ablations rather than scaling loss with parameter count. Appendix B reports qualitative routing analyses, not a claim-version loss measure.

untested.parts: Power-law loss form over several orders of magnitude with other resources non-bottlenecked; token and compute scaling.
Prediction of much larger runs from power laws fitted on small runs.
Loss-minimising parameter/token allocations across fixed compute budgets and their scaling exponents.
Loss sensitivity to architecture across a wide range at fixed total parameter count.
Power-law form outside text pretraining; image-generation quality comparisons do not establish that form.
Predictable downstream performance as a function of scale or pretraining loss.
Dependence of fitted exponents or compute-optimal splits on setup and fitting choices, and departures from a single power law.

record.verdict_notes: The recorded table values and baselines match the supplied text. Remove the V1 supports verdict: monotonic improvement alone does not establish a power law. Training exposure is matched within each depth, not across all depths: D12/D20 use 30,000 steps, D32 60,000. The approximately 20:1 compute-optimal ratio is cited from Hoffmann et al., not independently estimated. Image results and ablations are already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: The study reports BPB as memory slots and added parameters vary, but does not fit a power law or test its form over several orders of magnitude. It does not sweep training tokens or compute.

reader_labels.condition: Reported FineWeb-Edu text BPB results for MoVE memory sweeps in nanochat and MLA
reader_labels.reason: BPB decreases across the reported MoVE memory settings at fixed depth in these sweeps, but the tables do not establish a power-law shape; see r4-r7, r11-r13, r17-r18, r22-r27, and r31-r36.
